mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the logical disjunction “P ∨ Q” reflects a common misconception?

options.A: P ∨ Q is true when at least one of P or Q is true.
options.B: P ∨ Q is false only when both P and Q are false.
options.C: P ∨ Q is true when both P and Q are true.
options.D: P ∨ Q is false only when both P and Q are true.

mcqs.answer: P ∨ Q is false only when both P and Q are true.
mcqs.explanation: The disjunction P ∨ Q is false only when both components are false. Option D states the opposite, which is a typical misconception. Options A, B, and C are true statements about disjunction, while D incorrectly claims it is false only when both are true.

mcqs.question: If the implication P → Q is false, which of the following must be true about the truth values of P and Q?

options.A: P is true and Q is false.
options.B: P is false and Q is true.
options.C: Both P and Q are true.
options.D: Both P and Q are false.

mcqs.answer: P is true and Q is false.
mcqs.explanation: An implication P → Q is false only in the case where the antecedent P is true while the consequent Q is false. All other combinations make the implication true. Hence option A correctly identifies the required condition.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes when the biconditional P ↔ Q is true?

options.A: When P and Q have the same truth value.
options.B: When at least one of P or Q is true.
options.C: When both P and Q are true.
options.D: When both P and Q are false.

mcqs.answer: When P and Q have the same truth value.
mcqs.explanation: The biconditional P ↔ Q is true precisely when both statements are either true together or false together, i.e., they share the same truth value. Options C and D describe only part of the condition, while B is unrelated.

mcqs.question: What is the truth value of the compound statement (P ∨ ¬Q) → (P ∧ Q) when P is true and Q is false?
mcqs.explanation: For P = T and Q = F: ¬Q = T, so P ∨ ¬Q = T ∨ T = T. Also, P ∧ Q = T ∧ F = F. The implication T → F is false. Therefore the compound statement is false, making option B correct.

mcqs.question: The conjunction of two statements P and Q, denoted P ∧ Q, is true exactly when:

options.A: Both P and Q are true.
options.B: At least one of P or Q is true.
options.C: Both P and Q are false.
options.D: Exactly one of P or Q is true.

mcqs.answer: Both P and Q are true.
mcqs.explanation: A conjunction P ∧ Q requires both component statements to be true for the whole expression to be true. Any other combination makes the conjunction false.

mcqs.question: The disjunction P ∨ Q is false in which of the following cases?
mcqs.explanation: A disjunction is false only when both operands are false. Hence the combination where P is false and Q is false makes P ∨ Q false. All other combinations yield a true disjunction.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly defines the implication P → Q?

options.A: It is false only when P is true and Q is false.
options.B: It is true only when both P and Q are true.
options.C: It is false only when both P and Q are false.
options.D: It is true only when P is false and Q is true.

mcqs.answer: It is false only when P is true and Q is false.
mcqs.explanation: The implication P → Q is true in all cases except when the antecedent P is true while the consequent Q is false. Option A captures this definition precisely; the other options misstate the condition.

mcqs.question: A student says, “I will go to the park if and only if it is sunny.” Which logical expression represents this statement?
mcqs.explanation: The phrase “if and only if” denotes a biconditional relationship, meaning the two statements are equivalent. Therefore the correct representation is P ↔ Q. Options A and B represent one‑way conditionals, and D is a disjunction.
